route_note: The 2014 OpenCV gpu module is not built (texture references and cudaThreadSynchronize were removed from the CUDA runtime in CUDA 12, so canny.cu cannot be compiled against the real opencv2/gpu/device/common.hpp). modules/gpu/src/cuda/canny.cu (the record's file) and modules/core/include/opencv2/core/cuda_devptrs.hpp (PtrStep/PtrStepSz; unchanged by the fix) are copied byte-for-byte from ce42593f (buggy) and 7fd21d21 (fixed) with harness/r2_extract.sh (fixdiff.py RESULT PASS: blob sha1 of both files equals the commit blob; diff -r buggy fixed == the fix commit's diff, 4 added lines = 2 __syncthreads). Stubs in r2/common/opencv2/gpu/device/ (identical for both variants): common.hpp (cudaSafeCall, divUp, uchar typedefs, stand-ins for the removed texture<>/tex2D/bindTexture and cudaThreadSynchronize->cudaDeviceSynchronize), emulation.hpp (Emulation::smem::atomicAdd = ::atomicAdd), functional.hpp (unary_function/binary_function), transform.hpp (WithOutMask, TransformFunctorTraits, no-op transform()), utility.hpp (empty). The texture stand-ins and transform() are only reached from calcMagnitude/calcMap/getEdges, which the driver never calls; the kernel under test and its host launcher (canny::edgesHysteresisLocal, from the verbatim file) use none of them. The host main r2/common/driver.cu #includes the verbatim canny.cu.
driver: r2/common/driver.cu (no arguments): builds a 64x64 int edge map (0/1/2) in which every 16x16 tile has two vertical and two horizontal chains of 1s (columns 5 and 10, rows 4 and 11) crossing all warps of the block, seeded with 2 (top of column 5 / bottom of column 10 on alternating tiles, left end of row 4), calls canny::edgesHysteresisLocal(map, st) of the verbatim file, which launches edgesHysteresisLocalKernel<<<(4,4),(16,16)>>>, and compares the result with a host simulation of the step-synchronous (barrier-correct) 16-step flood fill; prints cells==2, mismatches, the stack-entry counter and a checksum; exit code 0.
input: 64x64 int map = 4096 cells, 16 blocks x 256 threads. Thread-level access estimate: each thread does about 4 global loads/stores and shared stores for the tile load, then 16 unrolled iterations of one own-cell read plus (only while the own cell is 1) 8 neighbour reads and at most 1 write; cells that are ever 1: 60 of 256 per tile. Upper bound 4096 x 16 x 10 = 6.6e5; expected about 1.5e5. Well below 1e7.
